newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: MALAYSIANS LOOK AT S.AFRICAN PETROCHEMICALS PLANT.
newsitem.headline: MALAYSIANS LOOK AT S.AFRICAN PETROCHEMICALS PLANT.

text.p: Malaysian companies are looking at the feasibility of a major petrochemicals plant in South Africa's Eastern Cape province, Deputy Trade and Industry Minister Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka said on Tuesday.
"The Malaysians are interested pending technical work which will inform their formal decision," she told Reuters.
"We expect that technicians from the two countries will be talking further as encouraged by the leaders."

She was responding to local radio reports saying that an agreement to build a $400 million refinery near East London had been signed during President Nelson Mandela's recent visit to Southeast Asia. She accompanied him on the trip.
"They did not sign an agreement," Mlambo-Ngcuka said.
Her written reply to Reuters did not specify if the Malaysians were interested in a refinery or petrochemicals plant, but an aide said it was the petrochemicals plant.

A petrochemicals plant in the relatively underdeveloped province has been mooted by several parties, notably by the Taiwanese in the lead up to South Africa's decision on whether to grant diplomatic recognition to China instead.
When South Africa opted for China, the Taiwanese pulled out of negotiations with a consortium of local private sector firms on the project.
But the consortium later said that the Taiwanese plan to build a world scale aromatics plant would not serve local needs.
The local companies approached included AECI, BP, Caltex, Engen, Hoechst SA, Polifin, Sasol, Sentrachem, Shell and Total.
